ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy resources? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy resources.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy resources.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Energy resources.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy resources.

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Keeping home? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Keeping home.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Keeping home.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Keeping home.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping home.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of water? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of water.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of water.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of water.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of water.

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Weather and Sky its resources? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Weather and Sky its resources.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Weather and Sky its resources.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Weather and Sky its resources.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Sky its resources.

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Exploring weather? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Exploring weather.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Exploring weather.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Exploring weather.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Exploring weather.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Harmful effects of? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Harmful effects of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Harmful effects of.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Harmful effects of.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Harmful effects of.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Exploring and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Caring for plants environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Caring for animals environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Managing waste environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — newton (N)

2. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy resources.

4. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Keeping home.

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of water.

7. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

8. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Sky its resources.

10. B — Producers

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Exploring weather.

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Harmful effects of.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Exploring; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Caring for plants environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Caring for animals environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Managing waste environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
